nodes.title: Number of differing positions

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be an array of length $n$ that is a permutation of $1, \dots, n$, and let $m(a)$ be the value that the program $\mathrm{minRearrange}$ computes on $a$. Then some unimodal permutation $x$ of $1, \dots, n$ differs from $a$ in exactly $m(a)$ positions, and every unimodal permutation of $1, \dots, n$ differs from $a$ in at least $m(a)$ positions. So $m(a)$ is the minimum number of positions in which $a$ differs…
nodes.title: Correctness of the unimodal rearrangement algorithm

nodes.summary: An array $a$ of natural numbers is unimodal if it is the concatenation of a strictly increasing array $b$ followed by a strictly decreasing array $b'$, where either part may be empty.
